notes: 9/12: inbound via blog signup (model pinning article). AE outreach - Jordan. high interest in deterministic code completions.
9/18: discovery call w/ Eng Lead (Priya Rao) + Head of Product (Samir Bose). Key ask: reproducible code completions across releases.
Quote: 'We need rollouts that can be pinned per-repo and a way to reproduce a completion exactly for debugging.'
They build an IDE copilot (VSCode + proprietary agent) that must match outputs in CI tests and allow canary comparisons across model versions.
Latency target: median editor-completion RTT <= 60ms (prefer <40ms) with streaming partial tokens.
Throughput: ~15k completion requests/day, bursty with peak at 200 rps during dev sprints.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for Dedicated if it guarantees reproducibility and support for rollouts.
Security: require SSO (SAML), audit logs for token-level actions, KMS for key management, retention controls for session code snippets.
9/25: sent security questionnaire (drive link). 9/27: SE call to review architecture (Carlos). Asked about model hash/manifest format for pinning.
Wanted: immutable model manifests + deterministic RNG seeding + model-config hashing so we can link a completion to a model version in bug reports.
They asked about eval gates: automatically block rollout if code-quality regressions detected by our test harness (unit test pass rate, lint drift, compile failures).
POC scope agreed: 2-week POC, baseline with hosted_api then short Dedicated trial to validate latency and reproducibility. Canary will be per-team (10% users).
Requested: example canary policy that pins model per-repo; ability to snapshot prompt templates + tokenizer/version metadata; logs must include model manifest id.
Notes: engineering team uses private monorepo; will need narrow VPC peering for repo access and a read-only webhook to push diffs for eval harness.
technical_requirements: Model/version pinning: per-repo and per-environment pinning; immutable model manifest ids in logs
Canary rollouts: weighted traffic split, per-team targeting, and automatic rollback based on eval gates
Eval gates: compare before/after on reproducibility tests (determinism), unit-test pass rates, compile success, and code-quality metrics
Deterministic outputs: support for seeded RNG, control of temperature/beam settings and explicit kernel selection reproducibility
Streaming: low-latency chunked token streaming with partial results in <40ms for first bytes in normal path
Prefix caching: ability to cache repo-level common prefixes to reduce inference cost and improve latency
Audit & observability: token-level traceability to model manifest id, per-request latency and cost breakdowns
Artifact retention: store model manifests and evaluation snapshots for at least 90 days for reproducibility audits
poc_milestones: Week 0: setup account, SSO, and VPC peering (read-only repo hooks)
Week 1: baseline hosted_api integration; enable streaming and model pinning; run reproducibility harness on 1k prompts
Week 2: spin up Dedicated pool (short trial), run canary (10% traffic), automated eval gates, compare latency and unit-test regressions
Deliverable: reproducibility report + recommended rollout policy + cost/latency tradeoffs
